extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, State and Federal Registration Agencies, State Apprenticeship Agencies, and administrators responsible for apprenticeship program registration and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and approval criteria for registering, operating, reviewing, and deregistering U.S. registered apprenticeship programs, including apprenticeship agreement contents, sponsor obligations, trainer/provider qualifications, EEO and recordkeeping requirements, end-point assessments, complaints, program reviews, and national standards development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include the identifying information of the parties, the occupation, and the duration of the apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as part of the required content items for every apprenticeship agreement; see additional required items below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — work processes and related instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must identify the work processes in which the apprentice will receive on-the-job training and the related instruction to be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties to the program's work process schedule and related instruction outline and supports assessment of whether the program provides requisite skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — apprenticeship term and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must state the length (term) of the apprenticeship and the schedule for on-the-job and related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be consistent with approved standards of apprenticeship and the work process schedule; used to verify completion requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — probationary period
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must specify a probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation rules differ during the probationary period (see cancellation provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — standards of performance and competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must specify the skills, competencies, or performance standards apprentices must achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should align with work process schedule and any National Occupational Standards or employer standards used by the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — wages and progression
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must specify the wage schedule, including starting wage, progressive increases, and any fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wage provisions must reflect program policies and legal requirements and are used to verify compliance and apprentice pay records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — hour requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must state the required hours of on-the-job training and related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These hour totals are used to determine completion and for recordkeeping of each apprentice's on-the-job and related instruction hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — training location and employer(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must identify the locations and participating employers where the apprentice will receive training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for determining participating employer obligations and for Registration Agency oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — processes for supervision and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must describe the supervision, training, and evaluation arrangements for the apprentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports assessment of trainer qualifications and monitoring of apprentice progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — supports to address barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must identify any efforts by the sponsor or partnering organization to address potential barriers to participation or completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include childcare, transportation assistance, and other supports to promote equitable participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — unreimbursed costs disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must disclose the nature and amount of any unreimbursed costs, expenses, or fees the apprentice may incur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures apprentices understand financial obligations associated with program participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — postsecondary credits/credentials information
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must describe any recognized postsecondary credits, credentials, or occupational qualifications the apprentice will or may receive upon successful completion, and any additional conditions for licensure or qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include description of any federal/state/local qualification or licensure requirements and additional apprentice obligations to obtain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — adherence to part 30 and State EEO plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties must state they will adhere to applicable requirements of part 30 and, where applicable, an approved State EEO plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms commitment to equal opportunity requirements applicable to registered apprenticeship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — related instruction pay and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must state whether apprentices are paid wages/fringe benefits during related instruction, the wage rate if paid, and whether related instruction is during work hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies compensation practices during classroom or related instruction components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — contact for dispute resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must provide contact information for the authority designated to receive, process, and make disposition of controversies or disputes that cannot be resolved locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, address, phone, and email if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — advanced standing/credit procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must include a description of the processes and procedures for granting advanced standing or credit consistent with §29.8(a)(20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how prior learning or experience may translate into credit or reduced term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-compete provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors or participating employers may not include non-compete provisions or other provisions restricting an apprentice's ability to compete or seek employment with another employer prior to program completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition applies whether in the agreement or imposed otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on non-disclosure provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors or participating employers may not include non-disclosure provisions that prevent a worker from working in the same field after employment or that restrict an apprentice from filing complaints with a Registration Agency or government body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors may include nondisclosure provisions limited to protection of confidential business information or trade secrets, subject to these restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of executed apprenticeship agreement to Registration Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors must submit a completed copy of the executed apprenticeship agreement for each apprentice to the Registration Agency within 30 days of execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission is required for registration records and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation during probationary period
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party may cancel the apprenticeship agreement during the probationary period specified in the agreement without cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation rules change after probationary period ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice-requested cancellation after probation
rubrics_metrics.description: After the probationary period, an apprentice may cancel the apprenticeship agreement at any time at the apprentice's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides apprentices continued autonomy post-probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor cancellation/suspension after probation for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: After probation, a sponsor may suspend or cancel an apprenticeship agreement only for good cause and must provide written notice to the apprentice explaining the cause and must notify the Registration Agency of the cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice to apprentice and RA is required whenever sponsor cancels; supports due process and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement — work process schedule and related instruction outline
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for registration, the sponsor must submit a work process schedule and related instruction outline consistent with an occupation deemed suitable for registered apprenticeship by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator may require a suitability determination if the submission substantially differs from previously approved frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement — standards of apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must submit the standards of apprenticeship for the proposed program as part of the registration application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards must be consistent with §29.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement — apprenticeship agreement submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must include the apprenticeship agreement for the apprenticeship program with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement must adhere to §29.9 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement — equitable recruitment and retention plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must submit a written plan for the equitable recruitment and retention of apprentices, including those from underserved communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewed under approval criteria and considered for provisional/permanent registration decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement — financial capacity and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must provide information showing they possess and can maintain the financial capacity and other resources necessary to operate the proposed program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency reviews financial capacity as part of approval criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement — disclosure of prior agency determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must disclose in writing all instances where a Federal, State, or local agency issued a final agency determination that the sponsor (or its officers/employees) violated applicable workplace or related laws, including description of violation and corrective actions taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by Registration Agency to assess risk and corrective steps; material to approval decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement — union participation provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If union participation in program operation exists or is provided for, a written acknowledgement of union agreement or lack of objection to registration is required; where no such participation is evidenced, sponsor must furnish application and program to the existing union and Registration Agency must allow 45 days for union comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures collective bargaining agents are informed and can comment prior to final registration action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement — description of EEO implementation steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must describe how it will implement affirmative steps to provide EEO in apprenticeship required by §30.3(b), including identifying responsible individuals, publication/posting of the EEO pledge, orientation schedules, recruitment sources, and procedures to prevent harassment and discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a multi-part requirement; see enumerated subrequirements for specifics (responsibility, posting, orientation, recruitment, anti-harassment).

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO plan content — responsible individual(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO description must identify the individual(s) responsible and accountable for overseeing the sponsor's commitment to equal opportunity in registered apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming accountable persons facilitates oversight and complaint handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO plan content — EEO pledge publication and posting
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO description must identify the publications or documents where the sponsor's EEO pledge will be published and the physical or digital locations where it will be posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visibility of the pledge is required to inform applicants, apprentices, and staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO plan content — orientation and information sessions schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO description must describe the planned schedule for orientation and information sessions for those connected with administration or operation of the apprenticeship program to inform and remind them of the sponsor's EEO policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include sessions for all apprentices and journeyworkers who regularly work with apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO plan content — recruitment sources list
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO description must provide a list of current recruitment sources that will generate referrals from all demographic groups within the recruitment area, including contact person, mailing address, telephone, and email for each source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates proactive recruitment from diverse sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO plan content — anti-harassment and complaint procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO description must describe procedures to ensure apprentices are not harassed or discriminated against and include: (A) planned schedule and content source for required anti-harassment training; and (B) procedures for handling and resolving complaints about harassment and intimidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific training and complaint-handling plans are required to demonstrate prevention and remediation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency review timeframe for complete applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete electronic application will be reviewed within 90 calendar days by the Registration Agency, which will approve the application if specified approval criteria are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Administrator determines a suitability determination is needed, timelines may be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — occupation suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency will approve applications only if the occupation covered by the proposed program has been determined by the Administrator to be suitable for registered apprenticeship training pursuant to §29.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator retains discretion to require suitability determinations when work process schedules substantially differ from previously approved frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — work process schedule provides specific skills and competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed work process schedule must provide training in the specific skills and competencies associated with the approved occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency evaluates whether the schedule adequately trains occupation-specific skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — portability of skills
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant's work process schedule and related instruction outline must provide apprentices with a portable set of occupational skills and competencies that are readily transferable between employers within the same industry or sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portability supports apprentices' employability across employers and locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — consistency with §29.8 standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards of apprenticeship submitted must be consistent with §29.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures program standards meet statutory/regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — apprenticeship agreement adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must adhere to the requirements of §29.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency checks agreement contents and prohibitions (e.g., non-compete/nondisclosure limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — sponsor financial capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The sponsor must possess the financial capacity and other resources necessary to operate the proposed program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial capacity is evaluated to ensure program sustainability and apprentice protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — addressing prior misconduct or violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agency will approve only if disclosures of past misconduct or violations show the issues have been satisfactorily addressed and cured and would not pose significant ongoing risk to apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must describe corrective actions taken; unresolved issues may prevent approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — union participation requirements satisfied
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, the union participation requirements described in the application provisions must be satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to satisfy union acknowledgement or notice requirements may affect approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criterion — satisfactory recruitment and EEO submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The sponsor's submission must be satisfactory with respect to the equitable recruitment and retention plan and EEO implementation description (paragraphs (a)(4) and (a)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RA reviews these materials substantively as part of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional registration and denial explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that meet required standards will receive a Certificate of Registration and provisional registration; if declined, the Registration Agency will provide a written explanation of why the application does not meet requirements and how deficiencies could be cured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants denied approval may resubmit consistent with subpart requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional program review within two years
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agency must review all provisionally registered programs for compliance within 2 years of registration or at the end of the first training cycle, whichever is sooner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome of review determines conversion to permanent registration or continued provisional status and potential deregistration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to permanent registration criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A program in compliance will be made permanent if the program's first full training cycle has been completed; if not completed, program remains provisionally registered through the first full training cycle for subsequent review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures programs operate as represented during initial training cycle before permanent status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration during provisional period for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A program not in compliance during the provisional registration period will be subject to deregistration procedures at §29.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional status subjects programs to early oversight and potential deregistration if deficiencies persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-permanent registration reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: After permanent registration, subsequent program reviews are conducted by the Registration Agency as provided in §29.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic reviews continue to ensure ongoing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum apprentice enrollment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registered apprenticeship program does not have at least one enrolled and participating apprentice registered with the Registration Agency, the Registration Agency may initiate deregistration proceedings, subject to limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions (not to exceed 1 year) include time between program registration and first apprentice registration, and time between a program graduating an apprentice and registration of next apprentice(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor proposals for modifications to standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor proposals for modifications or changes to standards or certified National Guidelines must be submitted to the Registration Agency, which must determine consistency with requirements and, if consistent, approve within 90 calendar days of a complete submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not approved, sponsor must be notified of reasons and provided appropriate technical assistance; approved changes recorded as amendments within 90 days of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program standards adoption agreement — employer obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A program standards adoption agreement must include a provision that the participating employer will adopt and comply with the sponsor's registered standards, comply with other applicable requirements in this part, and cooperate with and provide assistance to the program sponsor including apprenticeship-related data and records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes duties of participating employers to ensure program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of executed adoption agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each executed program standards adoption agreement must be transmitted to the Registration Agency by the sponsor within 30 days of execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing ensures RA awareness of participating employers and their obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension or cancellation of adoption agreement by employer
rubrics_metrics.description: A participating employer may cancel a program standards adoption agreement by providing 30 days' written notice to the sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides employers a mechanism to withdraw while giving sponsor notice for continuity planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor suspension/cancellation of adoption agreement for failure to satisfy obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A sponsor must suspend or cancel an adoption agreement if it determines the participating employer failed to satisfy the agreement's provisions; the sponsor must notify the employer, all affected apprentices, and the Registration Agency in writing explaining the reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suspension/cancellation interrupts training, sponsor must make reasonable efforts to place apprentices with another participating employer or program; failure to suspend/cancel when required may prompt RA deregistration proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of journeyworker trainers — mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: Journeyworkers providing on-the-job training must have a mastery of the relevant skills, techniques, and competencies of the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures trainers can teach occupation-specific practical skills effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of journeyworker trainers — up-to-date technical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Journeyworkers must have up-to-date knowledge of the latest advances in technical knowledge and skills necessary to maintain proficiency and expertise in the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainer ongoing professional development supports relevant instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of journeyworker trainers — communication and demonstration ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Journeyworkers must be able to effectively communicate and demonstrate specialized practical knowledge, work processes, skills, and techniques needed to acquire full proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes ability to teach through demonstration and explanation on the job.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of journeyworker trainers — objective evaluation ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Journeyworkers must be able to apply industry-recognized methods for objectively and fairly evaluating and monitoring apprentice progress and assessing attainment of competencies during on-the-job training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports fair and documented apprentice assessment and progress measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of journeyworker trainers — ability to relate instruction to job performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journeyworkers must be able to relate conceptual and theoretical knowledge from related instruction to successful performance of job-related tasks ordinarily performed in the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bridges classroom learning and workplace application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainer responsibility — safe and inclusive training environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainers must establish a safe and inclusive training environment that promotes effective apprentice development from all backgrounds, must have completed required anti-harassment training under part 30, and must not have a record of substantiated noncompliance with EEO requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainer conduct and training environment are part of compliance and may affect program standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of related instruction providers — faculty/certification/SME
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers of related instruction must, at minimum, serve as faculty/instructor at an accredited postsecondary institution, meet State certification requirements for vocational-technical instructors, or be recognized subject-matter experts (e.g., journeyworkers recognized within the industry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures related instruction providers have appropriate academic or industry credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of related instruction providers — teaching techniques training
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers of related instruction must have received previous training in teaching techniques and adaptable learning styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports effective classroom and adult-learner pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Occupational Standards approval criteria — occupation suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed National Occupational Standards set will be reviewed to ensure the associated occupation has been determined suitable for registered apprenticeship training by the Administrator pursuant to §29.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Administrator's review of proposed National Occupational Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Occupational Standards approval criteria — nationally applicable work process schedule framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed work process schedule framework must be documented as nationally applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures standards and schedules are portable and usable across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Occupational Standards approval criteria — nationally applicable curriculum framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed standards must include a nationally applicable curriculum framework for related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports consistency in related instruction across sponsors adopting the standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Occupational Standards approval criteria — nationally applicable evaluation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed standards must describe nationally applicable methods for conducting ongoing evaluations of apprentices, including development of nationally applicable end-point assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation methods and end-point assessments must be robust and comparable across programs adopting the standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and decision timelines for National Occupational Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator will solicit public comment for at least 30 days and make a determination within 90 days of submission for public comment (subject to extension) and will maintain a publicly available list of determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public input and timely determinations are required for standards transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Program Standards requirements — scope and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: National Program Standards must train apprentices for occupations not ordinarily subject to licensing, be national or multistate in design and scope, and satisfy applicable requirements of this part and part 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Programs are intended for occupations without prevailing licensing constraints and must meet regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Program Standards registration and reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: National Program Standards that meet requirements will be approved and registered nationwide by the Administrator; SAAs must accord reciprocal approval and registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator will provide written explanations if declining registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of National Program Standards with National Occupational Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Where National Occupational Standards exist, sponsors seeking registration of National Program Standards must use them but may modify them provided the Administrator determines the submission substantially aligns with the National Occupational Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications allowed only if substantial alignment is maintained as determined by the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards — requirements and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: National Guidelines must be national in applicability and scope, suitable for adoption/adaptation by State/local affiliates, satisfy applicable requirements, and may be recognized by the Administrator with a Certificate of Recognition; unfavorable determinations require written explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognized Guidelines serve as a basis for State/local program standards subject to local registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and periodic review of recognized National Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognized National Guidelines must be resubmitted for approval when amended consistent with §29.8(b) and every 5 years beginning on the date of most recent approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures guidelines remain current and aligned with standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-point assessment — arrangement prior to completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an apprentice's completion, the sponsor must arrange for an end-point assessment to objectively measure acquisition of the relevant knowledge, skills, and competencies necessary to demonstrate proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End-point assessments are required to validate attainment of occupational proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-point assessment — retake opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: An apprentice who is not successful on the end-point assessment must be offered at least one additional opportunity to complete the assessment at the apprentice's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports fairness and reasonable remediation opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-point assessment — accommodation notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The sponsor must inform all apprentices of their right to request a reasonable accommodation prior to administration of the assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures accessibility and compliance with accommodations requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Completion issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each apprentice whom the sponsor determines has successfully met on-the-job training and related instruction requirements and completes the end-point assessment will be awarded a Certificate of Completion by the appropriate Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate formalizes successful program completion and is issued by the RA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints — scope and EEO matters
rubrics_metrics.description: This complaints section does not apply to discrimination or EEO matters, which must be processed under part 30 or State EEO plans; non-EEO complaints regarding apprenticeship agreements or violations of this part may be submitted to the sponsor or Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes complaint channels depending on subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints — filing timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must be filed with the Registration Agency within 300 calendar days after the events giving rise to the dispute, though the RA may extend the filing time for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is required but relaxable for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint content and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All complaints must be submitted in writing by the complainant or authorized representative and must describe the dispute, including all relevant facts and documents, and must contain: (1) means of contacting the complainant or representative; (2) identity of the alleged responsible individual/entity; and (3) a short description of events, facts, circumstances, and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete, documented complaints allow prompt RA initiation of investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency investigation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The RA will acknowledge receipt in writing, initiate an investigation upon receiving a complete complaint, complete a thorough investigation developing a complete case record (interview lists/statements, document copies/transcripts, narrative report with exhibits), and provide written notification of findings to both respondent and complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RA must proceed expeditiously and maintain a comprehensive case record to support findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: RA protection of complainant identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency will protect the identity of the complainant to the extent practicable during investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality protections are applied except as necessary for investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RA obligation to attempt resolution when violation found
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an investigation indicates a violation of this part or the apprenticeship agreement, the RA will attempt to resolve the violation as expeditiously as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RA uses remedies and corrective plans to address violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to pursue other remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this complaints section precludes an apprentice from pursuing other remedies authorized under Federal, State, or local law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants retain concurrent legal remedies outside RA processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA alternative procedures with Administrator approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Apprenticeship Agency may adopt a complaint investigation procedure differing in detail from the given section provided it has been previously reviewed and approved by the Administrator pursuant to §29.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows SSAs procedural flexibility if approved by Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections against retaliation for complaint/participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants may not be intimidated, threatened, coerced, retaliated against, or discriminated against because they filed a complaint, opposed prohibited practice, furnished information or assisted in investigations, or otherwise exercised rights under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaliation protections are explicit and enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for sponsor permitting retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sponsor that permits retaliation and fails to remedy it will be subject to deregistration under §29.20(a) and other appropriate remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RA enforcement actions include deregistration for failures to address retaliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping obligation — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors and participating employers are responsible for maintaining records the Registration Agency considers necessary to determine compliance with this part and applicable laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records support program reviews, investigations, and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — employment decisions records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain records relating to employment decisions such as hiring/placement, promotion, demotion, transfer, layoff, termination, right of return from layoff, and rehiring of apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports review of nondiscriminatory employment practices and program operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — program operation information
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain information related to the operation of the registered apprenticeship program, including but not limited to standards, apprenticeship agreements, completion records, cancellation/suspension records, and compliance review files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core program documents must be retained and provided for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — apprentice performance and assessment records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain records pertaining to each apprentice's performance and progress in on-the-job training and related instruction, and records related to apprentice end-point assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary to verify attainment of competencies and completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — interim credential and milestone records
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, sponsors must maintain records pertaining to an apprentice's attainment of interim credentials, postsecondary academic credit, or other interim milestones attained during participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents progress and credentialing during the apprenticeship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — hours, wages, and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: For each apprentice, sponsors must keep records of the number of hours of on-the-job training, related instruction, total hours worked, and wages and fringe benefits paid for all hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to verify pay compliance and completion requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — non-EEO complaint records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain any records, including personnel records, applicable to non-EEO complaints filed with the Registration Agency pursuant to §29.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint documentation must be retained for investigations and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — safety records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain records related to the safety record of the sponsor and participating employers, including safety and health training provided to apprentices, incident logs required by occupational safety laws, and current worker's compensation documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety records help RA evaluate program compliance with workplace safety requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — part 30 required records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain any records required to be maintained under part 30 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrates EEO and other part 30 obligations into program records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — records required for veterans' educational assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain any records required under title 38, U.S. Code, so veterans and eligible individuals can use educational assistance for enrollment in registered apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports use of veteran education benefits for apprenticeship enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — records demonstrating compliance with Federal purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain any records demonstrating program compliance with registered apprenticeship requirements to meet Federal purposes as defined in the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures documentation for oversight and policy compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Records required by this part and other compliance information must be maintained for 5 years from the date of the making of the record or personnel action involved, whichever occurs later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to preserve complete and accurate records constitutes noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to records by Registration Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and participating employers must allow the Registration Agency access to records upon request for program reviews and investigations, including inspecting and copying books, accounts, records (including electronic), and any other material RA deems relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors must provide information about record formats and may be asked to provide electronic format details; information obtained will be used only for administration of this part or other applicable laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of records
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms, records, and other documents may exist in paper, electronic, or combination form, but regardless of medium they must be available and accessible for oversight and compliance purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors must ensure accessibility and readability of records in whatever format maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reviews — periodic frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: After permanent registration, the Registration Agency must conduct periodic reviews of the apprenticeship program not less frequently than every 5 years, except as described for other triggers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic reviews ensure ongoing compliance across program lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reviews — triggered reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agency must conduct reviews when it receives credible information or allegations that the program is not being operated in accordance with its standards or requirements, or at the Administrator's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trigger-based reviews allow prompt response to allegations of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reviews — consideration of relevant information
rubrics_metrics.description: In conducting program reviews, RAs may consider all information and data relevant to actual or potential noncompliance, including the program's performance under §29.25(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive evidence review supports accurate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor and employer cooperation during reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and participating employers must cooperate with requests for interviews or documentation and must not impede RA's ability to interview prospective, current, or former apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncooperation may affect review outcomes and enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Program Review Findings content
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of a program review, RA must present a written Notice of Program Review Findings identifying deficiencies, how to cure them, requirement to develop and submit a compliance action plan, and a statement that actions in §29.20 may be undertaken if compliance not achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be sent to the sponsor using contact information listed in registered standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor response timeline to Findings — compliance plan or rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: When sponsor receives a Notice indicating noncompliance, the sponsor must within 45 calendar days develop and submit a compliance action plan meeting specified requirements or submit a written rebuttal; RA may extend this deadline one time by up to 45 days for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely response is required; RA may provide extension for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance action plan content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A compliance action plan must include: (i) a specific written commitment to correct identified deficiencies; (ii) precise actions for each deficiency; (iii) time period for remediation and corrective program changes; and (iv) name(s) of individual(s) responsible for corrective actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must be specific, time-bound, and assign accountability for remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency responses to compliance action plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon evaluating the plan, the RA will either: (1) approve and determine program in compliance and terminate the review; (2) approve but continue review until implementation; or (3) reject the plan and work with sponsor to revise it or initiate deregistration under §29.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RA has three discrete response options depending on plan adequacy and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration remedies and steps by Registration Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: If RA determines sponsor or participating employer is not operating the program in accordance with requirements, RA must notify sponsor of specific violations and may: offer technical assistance, require submission of a compliance action plan, suspend sponsor's right to register new apprentices for a specified time, or deregister the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RA uses progressive remedies up to deregistration depending on severity and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration for cause — failure to correct or implement plan
rubrics_metrics.description: RA may deregister a program when it is not being operated in accordance with requirements and either has failed to correct specific violations identified or has failed to submit/implement an approved compliance action plan within required timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deregistration is enforcement for persistent noncompliance or failure to remediate.
